title: U.S. Treasury Sanctions Crypto Launderers Behind North Korea’s Fake Workers
text:
The U.S. Treasury sanctioned ten people and one entity, including two Russian crypto middlemen, for laundering money from North Korean fake IT worker schemes that fund its weapons programs.
The U.S. Treasury Department on Tuesday sanctioned ten individuals and one company, accusing them of helping North Korea collect wages from foreign employers, many of them American, through fake identities and forged paperwork.
The workers are typically placed at legitimate firms under invented personas, sometimes with AI-generated resumes, doctored photos, or deepfake video during interviews.
Most of their pay goes back to the regime, which Treasury says uses the money to fund its weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programs. Some of these workers have also gained access to corporate networks, where they have planted malware and taken proprietary data.
The sanctions focused less on the workers themselves than on the people who move the money. Two Russian nationals are at the center of the action.
Vitold Obertas, described by Treasury as a go-between for North Korean financial transactions, allegedly handled nearly $2 million in crypto conversions and at least $1.25 million in other currency transfers for North Korean officials since January 2025.
Ilya Boykov allegedly converted the equivalent of $3.5 million in crypto for Alis, a North Korean IT worker company that the U.S. sanctioned in 2024.
Two North Korean nationals, Kim Ki Hyok and Kim Hyo Dong, were also named for leading Russia-based worker delegations. Kim Ki Hyok has reportedly moved close to $500,000 in crypto for his team since 2024.
Treasury also sanctioned the First Financial and Technical Development Center, a North Korean-controlled entity operating in Russia, along with six workers who have generated more than $750,000 for it since 2025.
Treasury published wallet addresses on Ethereum and Tron tied to the sanctioned individuals, a signal to exchanges and other financial firms to watch for those accounts. One Ethereum address is linked to both Obertas and Boykov.
The action follows a March designation of a separate North Korean IT worker network, which Treasury said had laundered roughly $800 million in crypto for the regime. Australia and the European Union have also announced related designations this month, and Treasury coordinated the move with the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team.
Under the sanctions, any property these individuals or entities hold in the United States, or that is controlled by U.S. persons, is blocked and must be reported to the Office of Foreign Assets Control. Transactions with them are generally prohibited unless licensed, and companies owned 50 percent or more by blocked parties are subject to the same restrictions. Treasury warned that civil penalties can apply even when a violation was unintentional.
For companies that hire remote contractors, the advisories from the State, Treasury and Justice departments and the FBI offer guidance on spotting these schemes, including verifying identities, checking where payments are going, and watching for unusual access requests.

Russia Approves Securities Group To Oversee Crypto Exchanges
text:
The Bank of Russia approved NAUFOR as the country’s first self-regulatory organization for crypto exchanges and digital depositories.
The National Association of Securities Market Participants, known as NAUFOR, has won self-regulatory organization status for digital depositories and crypto exchanges. The Central Bank of Russia made the decision on October 29, according to Interfax.
The move turns a law into a working system. Russia’s framework, “On Digital Currency and Digital Rights,” passed the State Duma in July. It requires exchange operators and depositories to sit in central bank registries, and it requires them to join an SRO.
Interfax reports that the registry lists 23 crypto exchanges and eight digital depositories, including VTB, Sberbank, and units of T-Technologies, the holding company behind T-Bank. Firms on those registries have 90 days to join an SRO. In short, an SRO writes industry standards, monitors members, and represents the industry to regulators.
NAUFOR says it will help shape standards for digital asset markets and push the central bank on rule changes. Earlier in October, it received the same status for information system operators. The association has operated since 1996 and counts 725 members, including brokers, dealers, and fund managers from traditional markets.
JUST IN: 🇷🇺 Russia's central bank approved NAUFOR as a self-regulatory body for crypto exchanges and custodians. 👀Russia's new crypto law requires all registered crypto firms to join a self-regulatory organization within the next 90 days. pic.twitter.com/pchpFYg6KP
Traditional finance built NAUFOR’s model for stocks and bonds. Placing the same body over bitcoin exchanges and custody gives the state a familiar hand on the wheel.
Bitcoin Magazine reported in July that the law stops bitcoin from becoming money for everyday purchases. Domestic crypto payments stay banned. The law licenses exchanges and depositories, caps retail purchases, and opens a state-supervised channel for cross-border trade, a route that helps Russia move around Western sanctions.
The details matter for users. A depository would record holdings, and one reading of the framework lets it restrict transfers to personal wallets. Non-qualified retail buyers can purchase up to 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary, near $3,800.
Qualified investors face higher ceilings. These choices shape who can use the platforms and how.
Earlier this fall, the Moscow Exchange reportedly began testing cryptocurrency trading with professional market participants and planned to launch trading this December.
The exchange intended to use existing infrastructure and a partner digital depository following the introduction of Russia’s new cryptocurrency regulations in September.
Sberbank also received approval to custody Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, while President Vladimir Putin had previously acknowledged Bitcoin’s resistance to being banned.

title: Walmart Blocks Its Stock From OKX-ICE Tokenized Trading Venue - Decrypt
text:
The world’s largest retailer is now keeping its shares off OKX and ICE’s planned tokenized stock venue.
Walmart, Eli Lilly, Cigna Group, Carnival, and Arcos Dorados have objected to having their shares offered on OKXICE TSV, according to an updated notice from the venue dated Wednesday. The five additions bring the total to 38 companies.
That’s up from 33 a day earlier, when JPMorgan Chase, Coca-Cola and Dell were among seven newcomers. The tally has more than quadrupled since the venue’s first list of nine objectors on Oct. 15. It grew to 16 on Oct. 19, with names including Microsoft, and 22 on Oct. 23 when Wells Fargo joined the list.
The latest batch broadens the pushback beyond tech and finance into retail, health care, and travel. Arcos Dorados, the largest McDonald’s franchisee in Latin America, joins McDonald’s itself, which objected earlier this month. Eli Lilly and Cigna join UnitedHealth Group and Moderna among the health care companies on the list.
The objections carry real weight. Under the SEC’s innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate, a venue must notify a company before offering a version of its shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party.
If the company objects in writing within 30 days, the venue can’t make that stock available for trading, according to the SEC’s order. The objection applies only to that venue, and the notices don’t disclose the companies’ reasons.
OKXICE TSV, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX’s U.S. holding company, plans to let approved users trade tokenized U.S. stocks around the clock. OKX and ICE first teamed up on tokenized securities earlier this year before announcing the 24/7 venue this month.
Trades would run through permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on OKX’s XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC. The exemption caps the venue at 75 of the largest, most liquid stocks, with trading limited to 0.25% of each stock’s average daily volume, and up to 250 other stocks at 2.5%.
The list may not be finished. Under the SEC’s order, companies have 30 days from receiving notice to object, and some of the market’s most heavily traded names, including Nvidia, Tesla, Apple and Amazon, haven’t done so.
The venue has also said it can list shares tokenized by the issuers themselves, which would give companies direct control over how their stock appears onchain, though the notices don’t identify any such listings.

title: French Senate Adopts Bill for Automatic Sharing of Crypto Tax Data
text:
The French Senate adopted a bill authorizing the automatic exchange of crypto-asset tax information between international tax authorities, pending completion of the legislative process.
The French Senate adopted a bill to allow tax authorities to automatically exchange crypto transaction data with their foreign counterparts.
The bill passed its first reading on Tuesday and was then transmitted to the National Assembly as Bill no. 3421 for consideration.
The bill covers an agreement on exchanging crypto tax information and an update to an existing agreement on financial account information.
The crypto agreement is based on the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), developed by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). CARF sets common standards for participating jurisdictions to collect and automatically exchange information on crypto transactions.
France already introduced crypto reporting obligations through the 2025 Finance Act, implementing the crypto reporting amendment to the European Union’s Directive on Administrative Cooperation, known as DAC8. The rules require crypto service providers to report customer identities and transaction data to tax authorities, which share the information with authorities in users’ EU countries of residence.
French lawmakers are also debating crypto tax changes in the 2027 budget. The National Assembly adopted an amendment on Oct. 16 that would make gains from conversions into certain fiat-pegged stablecoins taxable from Jan. 1, 2027. The measure is not law yet.
Lawmakers resumed debate on the budget’s revenue section on Tuesday, with a vote scheduled for Nov. 3.
Related: ECB President Christine Lagarde to step down in February 2027
Tax reporting under DAC8 raises data security concerns because it involves sharing personal information, including names, addresses, tax numbers and transaction volumes, between EU tax authorities, Faustine Fleuret, global head of public affairs at lending protocol Morpho, told Cointelegraph.
The European Commission plans to create a central repository for crypto reports by the end of 2026. Each member state’s tax authorities would be able to access information concerning its tax residents.
Fleuret said that centralizing this information could create a “single point of failure” for sensitive crypto transaction data.
Share of wrench attacks by region. Source: CertiK
Fleuret’s remarks follow an alarming rise in physical attacks targeting cryptocurrency investors, also known as wrench attacks. During the first half of 2026, France accounted for 33 of the 52 verified wrench attacks worldwide, according to blockchain security company CertiK.
In a March incident, a French couple in their late 50s was robbed of about $1 million worth of Bitcoin by criminals posing as police officers.

title: Franklin Templeton Officially Launches 2 Bitcoin DRIP ETFs That Turn Dividends Into Bitcoin
text:
Franklin Templeton’s two Bitcoin DRIP ETFs, FBEQ and FIBT, started trading today on the Nasdaq.
Two Nasdaq-listed funds route dividends from large U.S. companies into a bitcoin sleeve that grows with every payment.
Franklin Templeton has officially launched two exchange-traded funds that convert stock dividends into bitcoin. The Franklin U.S. Equity Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF (FBEQ) and the Franklin U.S. Innovation Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF (FIBT) will trade on Nasdaq.
The launch completes the last regulatory step after Franklin filed registration papers with the Securities and Exchange Commission on October 22. The filings for both funds arrived in June without tickers or fees. Four months after that filing, the details are in.
FBEQ tracks the VettaFi U.S. Large-Cap 500 Bitcoin DRIP Index. The index holds the 500 largest U.S. companies by market capitalization, weighted by float-adjusted market cap. As of September 30, it held 499 stocks ranging from $10.2 billion to $5.5 trillion in size, with the heaviest concentration in information technology.
At inception, the index allocates 95% to those stocks and 5% to BTC. Each dividend the companies pay, whether regular or special, is reinvested into BTC at the market open on the day after the ex-date. The BTC share of the portfolio grows with each payment.
A traditional dividend reinvestment plan, or DRIP, uses cash dividends to buy more shares of the company that paid them. Franklin’s version routes that cash into BTC. For a holder, the dividend stream from the largest companies in America becomes a recurring BTC purchase, with no exchange account, no wallet and no custody decisions.
The bitcoin position has limits. At each quarterly rebalance, any allocation above 5% gets trimmed to 4.5%. If BTC exceeds 20% of the index between rebalances, the index cuts it to 4.5% within two business days, and the proceeds return to stocks.
The result is a stock fund with a bitcoin sleeve, a different product from a BTC fund.
The fund holds no BTC on-chain. It gains exposure through BTC exchange-traded products, including Franklin’s own spot fund, through bitcoin futures and options, or through depositary receipts, in some cases via a Cayman Islands subsidiary.

text:
Bitcoin's long-term holders are sitting on losses on about 4 million BTC bought between $85,000 and $118,000, and many may sell if the price climbs back toward that level, according to a note from on-chain analytics firm Glassnode.
Glassnode, which defines long-term holders as those holding coins for more than 155 days, said most of that block was bought in 2025. That block is worth about $326 billion at Bitcoin's current price of around $81,400, up 1.2% over the past 24 hours but about 35% below its all-time high of $126,080.
Glassnode said a band between $84,000 and $85,000 has turned Bitcoin back four times this year, and that the asset has closed above it on only five days since January. Bitcoin last broke above it in September, peaking at $87,100.
ETF holders are near break-even too. Glassnode puts the average price U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs paid for their coins at $81,500. Bloomberg Intelligence ETF analyst James Seyffart estimated the figure at just under $82,000 in a tweet on Wednesday, adding that Bitcoin has hovered around that level since the end of August.
Seyffart's chart put ETF holders' average unrealized loss at about $2.63 billion as of Monday. In replies, he said the estimate tracks only fund flows, not what secondary-market buyers paid.
The Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4.00% on Wednesday in a 10-2 vote, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike. Traders had put the odds of another quarter-point hike in December above 70% before the decision.
Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey, argued that a December hike had been priced in to a certain extent. "What truly constrains Bitcoin's performance," he told Decrypt, "is the persistently high U.S. Treasury yields and real interest rates, which are significantly raising the opportunity cost for investors holding risk assets."
The 10-year Treasury yield stood just under 5% at midday on Thursday, according to CNBC, down from 5.05% at Wednesday's close and a 52-week high of 5.37% on October 7.
Sun added that lower funding rates on Bitcoin perpetual futures have squeezed returns on cash-and-carry arbitrage, which pairs spot Bitcoin with short futures. Galaxy Research found that nine hedge funds and banks cut 68,000 BTC worth of spot ETF exposure as that trade dried up, while wealth platforms and sovereign funds added.
ETF flows have picked up this week. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $424 million from Monday to Wednesday, per SoSoValue data, after $635 million left the funds on October 22.
"Any rally above $85,000 could face selling pressure from long-term holders seeking to break even," Sun said, echoing Glassnode.
Both pointed to light selling, however. Glassnode said holders have realized smaller losses with each dip since August: at the August low, realized losses outweighed profits by about $630 million in a day, while around a dip on October 24 the largest daily net loss was about $27 million.
"The core issue facing the market right now is not panic selling, but rather insufficient new buying interest to support a sustained recovery," Sun said.
On the downside, Glassnode pointed to about $42 million in bids between $78,000 and $79,000 on Binance, and the average cost basis of newer buyers at $75,800.
Sun expects Bitcoin to keep trading between $75,000 and $85,000 in the short term until macro liquidity improves and ETFs resume continuous net inflows. Whether selling pressure near $85,000 can be absorbed "will serve as an important signal to determine whether the market can regain strength," he said.

title: $11 Billion in Bitcoin Options Expire Tomorrow—Here's What It Means - Decrypt
text:
About $11 billion in Bitcoin options expire on Friday on Deribit, a crypto options exchange, with Bitcoin trading near $81,500 a day after the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady while two of its officials voted to raise them.
Even people who never touch options have a stake, because the traders who sold these contracts must buy or sell real Bitcoin to hedge as the price moves, which can add to swings without any news behind them.
An option is a contract that gives its holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy (a call) or sell (a put) Bitcoin at a fixed price, called the strike, by a set date. Friday’s batch covers about 135,000 Bitcoin in contracts, roughly 88,700 calls and 46,500 puts, per Deribit’s data.
That equals about a third of all Bitcoin options open on the exchange and roughly 70% more than the $6.4 billion that expired in August. The put-to-call ratio, which compares bets on a drop with bets on a rally, is 0.52, so calls outnumber puts nearly two to one, which means there’s optimism in terms of price going up.
The $11 billion is notional value, the face value of the contracts at today’s price, not money changing hands. About 86% of the contracts are out of the money, meaning they would be worthless at current prices, and settling at today’s level would move roughly $130 million, about 1% of the headline figure.
Traders watch the Bitcoin options expiry day as one of the key events for their fundamental analysis. Another catalyst to consider is the Federal Reserve’s policy on rates. The Fed yesterday held firm at 3.75% to 4.00%, with expectations rising for another hike this year. Interest rates impact the whole economy as investment in risky assets and businesses would be less attractive than lending giving your money to the government through Treasuries.
Traders also watch max pain, the price at which the most contracts expire worthless and sellers pay out the least. Deribit’s open interest puts it at $78,000, about $3,500 below the market, though it describes positioning and does not predict where Bitcoin will settle. After all, this is crypto, and wild movements are not a strange occurrence.
The heaviest call bets sit at $95,000 and $100,000, about 16% and 23% above the current price, while the biggest put cluster is at $70,000, about 14% below. Friday’s expiry also saw the most trading of any Bitcoin options expiry on Deribit over the past 24 hours, with more than 6,000 contracts changing hands
Friday’s batch is smaller than the $15 billion expiry in March, but about three times the $3.6 billion expiry from April 2021.
The next test is December 25, when about 135,500 Bitcoin in options are already set to expire, roughly the same size as Friday’s and about two weeks after the Fed meets December 8-9.

title: Crypto Spends $176 Million on Midterms, But Only 13% of Voters See It as a Priority - Decrypt
text:
The crypto industry is spending heavily on next week’s midterm elections. Voters aren’t putting it near the top of their lists.
Only 13% of Americans say it’s extremely or very important that a political candidate supports the growth of emerging financial technologies like blockchain, crypto and decentralized finance, according to a survey conducted by Ipsos for the DeFi Education Fund, a crypto policy advocacy group.
A broader pitch fared better. About 35% say it’s very important that candidates ensure those building the next generation of financial technology are encouraged to do so in the U.S., the top-ranked policy position in the survey. Just 26% said the same about supporting new rules that allow innovation in the financial system.
The DeFi Education Fund describes the results as “bipartisan support for U.S. innovation,” and the narrower crypto question shows little partisan gap: 15% of Republicans and 13% of Democrats rate it very important. But on the top-ranked item, Republicans led Democrats 45% to 30%.
The survey polled 1,545 adults from Sept. 8 to 16 on Ipsos’ KnowledgePanel, the probability-based panel the Federal Reserve uses for its household finance survey, with a margin of error of plus or minus 2.8 percentage points. Party identification includes independents who lean toward a party.
The industry’s spending tells a different story. Crypto groups have spent about $176 million across more than 100 midterm races this cycle, according to a Reuters review, with super PAC Fairshake and its affiliates accounting for about $150.8 million through Oct. 20.
One Fairshake affiliate has disclosed more than $46 million in spending against former Sen. Sherrod Brown in Ohio’s Senate race.
The stakes are high for the industry after the Clarity Act, which would have set federal rules for crypto markets, failed a key Senate vote in September amid disputes over ethics provisions covering President Donald Trump’s crypto interests. Since then, the industry has turned to regulators like the SEC and CFTC to write the rules instead.
The survey suggests voters care more about security and control than about crypto itself. Some 63% say the financial system needs an upgrade to combat threats like AI and cybercrime, and 49% say the government shouldn’t decide which products they can invest in.

title: Home Miner Hits Bitcoin Jackpot: FutureBit Apollo Solo Finds Block Worth 3.154 BTC
text:
A miner operating through FutureBit’s Apollo Solo setup found Bitcoin block 973,262 earlier this week, collecting the full reward of 3.154 BTC plus fees from 2,477 transactions. Multiple explorers, including mempool.space, list the finder as “FutureBit Apollo Solo,” and the coinbase transaction includes text referencing FutureBit and Apollo.
FutureBit posted about the find on X: “Gradually, then suddenly. We (the people) hit a Bitcoin block today. Bitcoin belongs in the hands of sovereign individuals. And we’re building to keep it there.” The company stated that an Apollo device or Solo Node running its built-in solo pool assembled the block template, served the work, and submitted the completed block to the network. The public record does not identify the exact hardware or hashrate that produced the winning hash. It could have been an Apollo BTC, Apollo II, Apollo III, or other compatible machines pointed at a Solo Node, according to FutureBit’s account of the block.
This marks at least the fourth block attributed to FutureBit Apollo Solo. Earlier ones include blocks 867,760, 881,423, and 888,737. FutureBit designs its Apollo hardware for operators who want to run a full Bitcoin node and mine independently at home rather than through large commercial pools. The most recent model, the Apollo III, is rated for up to 18 TH/s in turbo mode with an integrated full node. Bitcoin Magazine covered the Apollo III launch in February 2026 and previously examined FutureBit’s approach to home mining in a July 2025 piece.
Solo mining, is often called lottery mining because of the low odds relative to the size of the reward, remains uncommon against a network hashrate that has recently sat near 1,070–1,087 EH/s. A home-scale setup in the 10–18 TH/s range still faces expected times to a block measured in centuries under current difficulty, yet verified solo finds continue to appear on-chain. Bitcoin Magazine examined the mathematics of these odds in an article titled Why Bitcoin Lottery Mining Has Better Odds Than The Powerball. It compared continuous Bitcoin block attempts with the much lower frequency of major lottery draws.
Another solo block was found the following day via CKPool Solo, illustrating that individual operators can still capture full rewards even as industrial pools produce the large majority of blocks. For users running FutureBit hardware, the company notes that the individual users control both the node and the solo pool, retaining the full reward when a block is found. Solo mining also has significant privacy benefits, and hardware and energy costs can be written off against taxes in some jurisdictions.
The October 26 block is one more validation that solo mining can be viable. Satoshi Nakamoto’s original Bitcoin design intended the full Bitcoin node to be able to mine blocks, not just validate and audit the blockchain. Improvements in hardware and mining optimizations later on led to the creation of mining pools, which created a very competitive and industrial mining sector. The secondary effects of industrial Bitcoin mining, such as reliable energy demand that can stabilize the grid, have been a boon for states like Texas.
However, the dream of bringing mining back to homes and end users remains alive through companies like FutureBit, Bitaxe, and HeatBit, among others, that are converting heating appliances into Bitcoin miners or designing hardware of the sort for the home.

title: Hackers Publish Work Details of 41,000 Homeland Security Employees - Decrypt
text:
Names, job titles, office locations, and phone numbers for more than 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees and contractors were published online Wednesday by a transparency nonprofit.
The nonprofit says a hacktivist group, meaning hackers driven by politics rather than profit, gave it the records.
The department oversees border protection, immigration enforcement, and cybersecurity, so the file works like a directory of who does what, who reports to whom and how to reach them.
Transparency groups say the contact details are useful for public-records requests. Security researchers warn the same list could help anyone who wants to impersonate a supervisor over the phone or work out who sits behind a sensitive investigation.
The nonprofit, Distributed Denial of Secrets, publishes leaked documents and calls this dataset Icepick. It says the hackers, who call themselves the Department of Peace, took the records from an Okta single sign-on service used by DHS, a login system that lets employees open many internal tools with one account.
Okta, the company behind that login service, disputes the claim. “Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised,” the company told Reuters.
The group says it acted after Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin pledged stepped-up operations by Immigration and Customs Enforcement, known as ICE. “On July 17th, Markwayne Mullin said he was ‘turning up the heat.’ This is what happens to ICE when you do that,” a spokesperson for the group said. “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs,” the hackers wrote.
The searchable archive indexes 41,191 people, including 21,329 from Customs and Border Protection and about 10,000 from ICE, a third of them in its investigative arm, Homeland Security Investigations.
It also lists more than 55,000 internal permission groups, which are labels that control who can open which systems, along with each person’s name, title, office, email, phone number and manager. DDoSecrets co-founder Emma Best says the dataset contains no home addresses.
“DHS is aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively,” a department spokesperson said.
DHS has also filed a takedown notice through the security firm ZeroFox, asking the domain registrar to stop serving contact and location data of people who did not consent to its publication. The search site built on the data stopped loading Thursday, with its domain showing a registrar hold, and Bluesky is blocking links to the nonprofit hosting the archive.
In September, the cybercrime group ShinyHunters claimed to hold 2 to 3 terabytes of data on FBI agents and job applicants, and the bureau told staff to assume hackers have their personal data.
The newest records in the archive date to August 19, and some entries, including CISA staff who have since left the agency, are already out of date.

title: Blockchain industry revenue shifts toward publicly traded firms
text:
A new 1kx report finds that public companies are capturing a larger share of blockchain revenue, driven by institutional adoption and real-world applications.
Publicly traded companies accounted for 16% of blockchain industry revenue in 2026, more than double their 7% share in 2022, according to a new report from crypto investment firm 1kx.
The increase comes as overall blockchain revenue is projected to decline 28% year over year to roughly $100 billion in 2026. The report analyzed data from more than 2,600 protocols and earnings reports from 104 publicly traded companies through the third quarter.
The researchers attributed the growing share of public companies partly to new stock market listings, including stablecoin issuer Circle, which went public in 2025, and revenue growth among existing companies. The 10 largest publicly traded companies in the study doubled their blockchain-related revenue over the past three years.
Coinbase and Circle generated approximately $3.3 billion in combined blockchain-related revenue in the first half of 2026, according to 1kx, while publicly traded Bitcoin miners earned roughly $2 billion. Traditional financial firms, including JPMorgan, BlackRock, CME Group, Visa and Robinhood, accounted for another $1.1 billion collectively.
Revenue remains concentrated among a relatively small number of businesses. The six largest publicly traded companies accounted for roughly 50% to 60% of the group’s revenue, according to the report.

title: Chrome Can Now Pull Details From Your Gmail to Fill Out Web Forms - Decrypt
text:
Google’s Chrome browser can now pull personal details from your Gmail inbox to fill out online forms for you, the company said in its announcement on Wednesday.
The update, called “enhanced autofill,” suggests order numbers, tracking information, and flight bookings when a form asks for them, wrote Amanda Lim, a Chrome product manager, in the announcement. Autofill is the browser tool that types in details like your name and address so you don’t have to.
It runs on Gemini, Google’s AI assistant, through a feature called Personal Intelligence, which lets Gemini draw on connected apps such as Gmail and Google Photos to tailor its answers to your own life. It is rolling out to Gemini in Chrome users who have Personal Intelligence turned on, on desktop, Android and iOS, starting in the U.S.
Google’s post names only those three kinds of data as coming from Gmail. Credit card numbers and addresses are part of Chrome’s standard autofill, which fills them from details you have saved in the browser, and the announcement does not say the new feature pulls them out of your inbox.
“You can manage whether enhanced autofill is enabled and what it can access via your Chrome settings,” Lim wrote. “As always, sensitive data is encrypted and you remain in control.”
Encryption scrambles data so only Google and other authorized parties can read it, though the post does not explain how that applies to the Gmail content Chrome reads or what it scans.
“Built with privacy in mind, Gemini and AI Mode don’t train directly on your Gmail inbox or Google Photos library,” Google said in March, when it began expanding Personal Intelligence to free U.S. users. AI Mode is Google’s AI-powered experience inside Search.
Users choose whether to connect their apps and can switch the connections off at any time, the post says, though Google does train on limited information, such as specific prompts and the model’s responses.
In November, users pushed back on a Smart Features setting that let Gemini analyze emails and calendars unless they opted out, and Google said it had not changed its underlying data-handling practices.
Google also revised its privacy policy effective Oct. 16, adding an exception to its pledge not to use Gmail, Drive, and Photos content for ads: personalized ads can draw on that data if users choose to make it available to other Google services that support them. Google says the content is not used for ad targeting by default and that advertisers do not get access to the contents of Gmail, Drive, or Photos.
Chrome has about 65% of the browser market, and in January Google gave paying U.S. subscribers an AI browsing agent called auto browse, which clicks through websites and fills out forms on a user’s behalf.
Chrome also dropped a line from its settings saying on-device AI, meaning models that run on your own computer rather than Google’s servers, works without sending data to Google servers. Google said the wording change did not reflect a change in how it handles on-device AI.
The rollout began Wednesday in the U.S. on desktop, Android and iOS, and Google’s announcement gives no date for other countries

Total revenue came in at $1.22 billion, in line with expectations, flat from the second quarter and down 35% from a year earlier. Transaction revenue slipped 1% to $590 million but beat the roughly $527 million analysts expected, as crypto volatility sank to multiyear lows and trading volume across the market fell.
The standout was prediction markets, which crossed $200 million in annualized revenue, making it one of the fastest-growing products in Coinbase’s history, the company said.
Daily traders grew more than 60% from the prior quarter, and revenue has compounded 82% per quarter since launch. CEO Brian Armstrong said the product kept “growing even through slower sports months.”

Paid Coinbase One subscribers reached an all-time high, up 24% from a year earlier, and the exchange’s share of global crypto trading volume rose to 10.7%, its fourth straight quarterly gain.
“Prediction markets are adding another revenue stream and are less correlated to crypto volatility,” CFO Alesia Haas said.
Coinbase also cut its 2026 adjusted expense guidance by another $100 million at the midpoint, to between $4.15 billion and $4.3 billion, following cost reductions in May. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 60% from the prior quarter to $333 million. Through Oct. 25, fourth-quarter transaction revenue stood at about $165 million.
The positive results follow two consecutive losing quarters. Coinbase posted a $394 million loss in the first quarter and missed estimates in the second as trading activity slowed, though analysts said at the time they weren’t worried about the stock’s slide.
Shares closed Thursday at $160.59, down 1.1%, before the results came out, and were little changed in after-hours trading. The stock is down more than 55% from its 52-week high of $361.40.

text:
At least $5.57 billion in crypto has left wallets linked to Binance across three blockchains in what appears to be a breach of the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange.
If confirmed as a hack, it would be the biggest crypto hack on record. Binance has not confirmed its exchange has been hacked but said it is aware of the “potential security issue and is actively investigating.”
“We have not confirmed any impact to user funds,” the company posted on X. “Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information.”

Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official… pic.twitter.com/dN76yhzYM0
— Binance (@binance) October 29, 2026
Binance is the world's largest crypto exchange, where millions of people buy, sell and store their coins. The money came from its hot wallets, the internet-connected wallets exchanges use to process customer withdrawals.
The tally counts $3.51 billion on Ethereum, $1.44 billion in 18,270 Bitcoin and $630 million on Tron. The first Ethereum transaction, at 20:24 UTC, sent 167,464 ETH plus 63 token transfers to a brand-new address, including 1.615 billion USDT, a stablecoin built to always trade at $1, according to Etherscan.
Three minutes earlier, an address funded through Tornado Cash, a mixer that scrambles the trail of crypto payments, submitted a delegation for a Binance hot wallet using EIP-7702, an Ethereum feature that lets an ordinary wallet run smart-contract code. “7702 lets a normal wallet execute delegated code. The delegation persists; that code can authorize later transfers without another signature from the wallet,” Odysseas Lamtzidi, founder of Phylax Systems wrote on X.
1/4 EIP-7702 can turn the wallet itself into the sweeper.
A Binance-labeled wallet moved 167,464 ETH + 63 tokens, including 1.615B USDT, just 3m24s after a signed delegation was installed.

— Odysseus | phylax.systems (@odysseas_eth) October 29, 2026
How the attacker got the required signature is still unknown. Tether froze 975.1 million USDT in the main receiving address, and Circle, issuer of the rival stablecoin USDC, froze 823 million USDC in the same wallet at 21:04 UTC, bringing the total frozen to about $1.8 billion. Both issuers can block specific addresses from moving their tokens, but the attacker is moving funds fast.
"Circle is closely tracking reports of a potential exploit involving Binance," Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire posted on X. "In coordination with law enforcement, we have frozen more than 800M USDC associated with the incident and will continue supporting the investigation."
Total on the hack is at least $5.57B across 3 chains (likely more)

Binance lost 7,000 Bitcoin, about $40 million, in a 2019 hack. The $5.57 billion tally would be more than triple the roughly $1.5 billion Bybit heist in February 2025, the previous record.

title: Binance Hacker Hunts for Exit Ramps as DeFi Exchanges Pause Markets - Decrypt
text:
The attacker behind the wallets draining Binance is using decentralized exchanges such as Uniswap and Aave as exits, swapping stablecoins that issuers can freeze for Ethereum that nobody can, according to Etherscan records for 10 wallets, eight of them labeled as exploiters.
Earlier today, wallets linked to the world’s largest crypto exchange were drained of at least $5.5 billion, with the total tally still climbing. The company said it was investigating the security incident but did not confirm user funds were affected, though security experts widely believe the exchange was indeed hacked.
Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle moved quickly to blacklist the suspected attacker’s addresses in order to freeze a portion of the funds and make them inaccessible. As centralized issuers, they each have the ability to blacklist addresses so their tokens cannot move, and more than $2 billion of those two tokens have been frozen so far by different stablecoin providers. ETH has no issuer, so every dollar converted before a freeze lands is out of their reach.
The swaps run through Uniswap, a decentralized exchange where trades settle automatically with no company in the middle.
One relay wallet received 20,940 ETH ($45.58 Million) from Uniswap’s UniswapX contract at 20:34 UTC, another got 3,552 ETH (over $8 million) at 20:47, and two later wallets took in about 18,085 ETH (around $41 million) from Uniswap contracts, in 7,444 ETH and 10,642 ETH batches, and about 16,498 ETH ($37.5 million), in 6,946 ETH and 9,552 ETH batches.
Aave, a lending app where users deposit crypto as collateral to borrow other coins, offered a second exit. Between 20:57 and 21:01 UTC, one wallet deposited $10 million and then $50 million in USDT and borrowed 3,271 ETH ($7.43 million) and then 16,491 ETH ($37.47 million) against it, which prompted cybersecurity experts Odysseas Lamtzidi, founder of Phylax Systems, to warn of “contagion in full effect.”

The ETH is piling up rather than moving on. “Ripple is closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and its attackers’ RLUSD holdings and we are actively freezing affected funds,” Jack McDonald, Ripple’s senior vice president for stablecoins, said in a statement. “We’re coordinating with relevant parties and stand ready to support any investigation and appropriate action to keep users protected.”

title: Strategy (MSTR) Posts Record Operating Income In Q3 2026
text:
Strategy reported record $20.91 billion in Q3 2026 operating income, driven by Bitcoin’s rebound, despite declining revenue, negative year-to-date BTC yield, and continued pressure to fund preferred dividends.
Strategy posted the largest operating income in its history on Thursday, booking $20.91 billion for the third quarter of 2026. Most of that total came from a paper gain on the company’s bitcoin stack.
Net income reached $19.53 billion, or $44.75 per diluted share, up from $2.79 billion a year earlier.
Chief Financial Officer Andrew Kang, who announced his departure in the same release, framed the result plainly: “Q3 operating income of $21 billion was the largest ever in Strategy’s history.”
Strategy marks its bitcoin to market each quarter, so every price move flows into earnings. Bitcoin rallied during the period. The company’s 848,517 bitcoin were worth $68.9 billion as of October 23, when the token traded at $81,200. The holdings carry an average cost of $75,446, which leaves the position in the black on paper.
Kang pointed to the purchases as the engine of the quarter, saying the company “increased our bitcoin holdings by 26% year-to-date in a challenging bitcoin market.”
Total revenue fell 3%from a year ago to $125.4 million, below analyst estimates of $127.2 million. Gross profit came in at $89.6 million, a 71% margin compared with 70% a year earlier. The company ended September with $2.50 billion in cash and equivalents and $3.40 billion in short-term investments.
Bitcoin per share, the metric management uses as its main yardstick, moved the other way. The BTC yield stands at negative 3.7% for the year, meaning each share holds less bitcoin than it did in January. Measured in dollars, the bitcoin position shows a $2.03 billion loss over the same period. To fund preferred dividends and stock buybacks, the company has sold roughly $431.8 million of bitcoin this year, a figure the release puts at approximately that amount.
Strategy raised $21.23 billion of capital in 2026, including $5.41 billion in net proceeds from its at-the-market program during the third quarter alone. The company then spent a large part of that money on its own preferred stock. It repurchased 20,980,508 shares of STRC for $2.04 billion at an average of $97.39 per share, a discount to the $100 stated amount.
Chief Executive Phong Le said the buyback program was meant to put the security on firmer footing: “Strategy demonstrated its commitment to returning STRC to health.” Management said it intends to keep buying while STRC trades below par, and about $956.7 million remains under the authorization.
The company’s dollar reserves now total $5.07 billion, made up of a $4.83 billion USD Reserve and $242.4 million of USD Cash. Strategy says that cushion covers 3.4 years of dividend and interest obligations. The board kept the STRC dividend rate at 12.00% to support trading near the $100 stated amount.
Shareholders approved a move to daily dividends on October 28. STRC begins paying daily on November 1, and STRF, STRK, and STRD follow on January 1, 2027.
Le framed the change as a step toward a different kind of market: “Daily dividends are a natural step toward the tokenized, 24/7/365 financial system. Digital Credit is being built for that world, and Strategy intends to lead it.”
Strategy also expects its preferred distributions to count as a non-taxable return of capital for ten years or more, because it does not expect positive accumulated earnings and profits. Shareholders should consult their own tax advisers.
That said, Strategy’s STRC stock is nearing $100. Earlier today, STRC reached $99.99 which once par would reopen funding for Bitcoin purchases. As mentioned ealier, shareholders approved daily dividends to improve liquidity and reduce price volatility. That said, Strategy has not yet confirmed a restart of STRC share issuance.
